title: IntervalArray.__new__ must pass only ndarrays to Cython intervals_to_interval_bounds (RangeIndex / non-interval EA input)
answers: TypeError: Argument 'intervals' has incorrect type (expected numpy.ndarray, got RangeIndex)
IntervalIndex union with empty RangeIndex / pd.DataFrame().index fails
pd.IntervalIndex(pd.Index(['a'], dtype='string')) gives an unhelpful error instead of 'is not an interval'
body:
Symptom: building an IntervalIndex, or calling astype("interval"), from a RangeIndex or a non-interval ExtensionArray (masked Int64/Float64, arrow, string, datetimelike, sparse) raised `TypeError: Argument 'intervals' has incorrect type (expected numpy.ndarray, got ...)`. This also broke IntervalIndex set ops with an empty RangeIndex, e.g. `pd.DataFrame().index`.
Root cause: pandas/core/arrays/interval.py:IntervalArray.__new__ passed data straight to the Cython `intervals_to_interval_bounds`, which only accepts np.ndarray. `extract_array(..., extract_numpy=True)` leaves a RangeIndex as it is, and `_maybe_convert_platform_interval` can still return an EA.
Fix pattern: call `extract_array(data, extract_numpy=True, extract_range=True)`, then, after `_maybe_convert_platform_interval`, run `np.asarray(data)` on any remaining ExtensionArray before the Cython call. Empty or all-NA input now gives an IntervalIndex of NaN that matches the numpy-backed equivalent (all-NA Int64 gives an interval[float64] subtype). Any other input raises the usual TypeError "... is not an interval".
Constraints: make the conversion in the constructor itself, not in `_maybe_convert_platform_interval`. That helper also serves `IntervalArray.from_breaks`, which has to keep EA breaks intact (an earlier attempt, GH-68345, special-cased RangeIndex there instead). Any new Cython helper call in this module needs the same ndarray coercion.
applies: pandas/core/arrays/interval.py IntervalArray constructor and anything that converts non-interval input to IntervalArray (IntervalIndex(), astype('interval'), set ops)
